newsitem.title: UK: Bass hopes for speedy decision on merger.
newsitem.headline: Bass hopes for speedy decision on merger.

text.p: Brewer-to-leisure group Bass Plc said it hoped the government's Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) can decide quickly whether to allow its proposed merger with Carlsberg-Tetley to go ahead.

"We had always known that a referral was a possibility and were prepared for it," said a Bass spokeswoman. "The continued uncertainty is very unsettling for employees of both businesses and we remain convinced of the benefits to all concerned of the merger proceeeding as swiftly as possible," she added.
Earlier, Ian Lang president of the Board of Trade announced the referral of the proposed Bass takeover to the MMC which is due to report on its investigation by March 24, 1997.
Brian Revell, Transport and General Workers Union national secretary for the drinks industry, welcomed the decision to refer the Bass takeover.
"Our main concern is that if the takeover is allowed to proceed, at least 2,000 jobs are likely to be lost," he said in a statement.

"However, we acknowledge that the situation is complicated and there is a possibility of a lesser number of jobs being lost if the takeover does go ahead due to the competitive pressures in the industry."
